engine.definition: The machine in a vehicle that produces power to move it.

clutch.definition: A mechanism that connects or disconnects an engine from the transmission.

carburetor.definition: A device in some engines that mixes fuel with air before combustion.

crankshaft.definition: A shaft that converts the pistons' movement into rotation.

camshaft.definition: A rotating shaft that controls when an engine's valves open and close.

hood.definition: The hinged cover over a car's engine compartment.

bumper.definition: A part fitted to the front or rear of a vehicle to help absorb minor impacts.

roof.definition: The top outer part of a vehicle's body.

dashboard.definition: The panel in front of the driver that contains instruments and controls.

pedal.definition: A foot-operated control used to accelerate, brake, or operate the clutch.

console.definition: The section between the front seats that holds controls and storage.

spring.definition: An elastic metal part that compresses or stretches to absorb forces.

alignment.definition: The adjustment of wheel angles so the vehicle travels as intended.

coolant.definition: A fluid that carries heat away from an engine to help prevent overheating.

gas.definition: Gasoline used as fuel in a vehicle's engine.

refrigerant.definition: A substance that carries heat through an air-conditioning system.

hatchback.definition: A car with a rear door that opens upward to access the cargo area.

convertible.definition: A car with a roof that can be folded or removed.

suv.definition: A passenger vehicle with a taller body and higher ground clearance than many cars.

sports-car.definition: A car designed for responsive handling and strong performance.

luxury-car.definition: A car that offers a high level of comfort, finish, and features.

van.definition: A road vehicle with an enclosed body for carrying people or goods.

electric-car.definition: A car powered by an electric motor using energy from a battery.

hybrid.definition: A car that uses both a fuel-powered engine and an electric motor.

hearse.definition: A vehicle used to carry a coffin to a funeral or burial.

lot.definition: An outdoor area where a dealership parks and displays vehicles.

reception.definition: The area where visitors are welcomed and directed to staff.

test-drive.definition: A short drive taken to assess a vehicle before buying it.

lease.definition: An agreement to use a vehicle for a set period in exchange for payments.

down-payment.definition: The initial amount paid toward a purchase before the remaining payments.

used.definition: Previously owned or operated by someone else.

demo.definition: A vehicle used by a dealership to demonstrate a model to customers.

mileage.definition: The distance a vehicle has traveled, measured in miles or kilometers.

technician.definition: A trained worker who diagnoses and repairs vehicle faults.

stop-sign.definition: A road sign requiring drivers to come to a complete stop.

crosswalk.definition: A marked area of a road designated for pedestrians to cross.

curb.definition: The raised edge separating a road from a sidewalk.

underpass.definition: A road or pedestrian passage that runs beneath another route.

brake.definition: To slow or stop a vehicle using its brakes.

steer.definition: To control the direction in which a vehicle moves.

signal.definition: To use an indicator or another signal to show an intended maneuver.

overtake.definition: To pass a vehicle traveling in the same direction.

insurance-claim.definition: A request to an insurer for payment or coverage under a policy.
